$description: Polytope tokens. Primitives hold raw values; semantic tokens point at primitives and change per theme. Edit here, then run `npm run build`.

white.$description: Gallery white. The light page ground, the light chart surface, and white text on black.

50.$description: Panel chalk. Text inside black panels and code blocks.

100.$description: Gallery wall. Sunken surfaces and table stripes.

200.$description: Hairline gray. Rules between table rows and list items, and chart grid lines.

300.$description: Panel gray. Muted text inside panels, and muted text in dark mode.

500.$description: Quiet gray. Placeholders and the quietest labels on white, still above 4.5:1.

600.$description: Caption gray. Captions, metadata, and inactive tabs; the hairline inside panels.

700.$description: Rules between rows in dark mode.

800.$description: After-hours panel. Panels in dark mode, one step lighter than the ground.

900.$description: Sunken surfaces and the chart surface in dark mode.

950.$description: Exhibit black. Panels, heavy rules, body text.

100.$description: Pale tomato tint. Not used by the kit; for your own tinted backgrounds.

400.$description: Tomato bright. The accent in dark mode and the code keyword color.

500.$description: The moving part: current location, the balls in the probability machine.

600.$description: Tomato ink. Tomato as text on white, and the hover fill of primary buttons.

100.$description: Mustard soft. The quiet note fill in light mode.

400.$description: Mustard light. The focus ring inside panels and in dark mode, and the code comment color.

500.$description: Notes and highlights. Always carries black text.

700.$description: Deep mustard. Not used by the kit; for mustard text or marks on white.

100.$description: Pale teal tint. Not used by the kit; for your own tinted backgrounds.

300.$description: Teal light. Links in dark mode and inside panels, and the code string color.
Sequential chart ramp, step 3; also the code number color.

500.$description: Cobalt. Sequential chart ramp, step 5, and the third categorical chart slot.

surface-sunken.$description: Recessed areas: table stripes, inline code, input wells.

panel.$description: Exhibit panel. Code blocks, the probability machine, demo canvases.

panel-text.$description: Text inside black panels and code blocks.

panel-rule.$description: Hairlines inside panels, such as the rule under a code bar.

text-subtle.$description: Placeholders and the quietest labels. Still above 4.5:1 on the page ground.

rule-strong.$description: The 3px exhibit rules and control borders.

rule.$description: Hairlines between rows and list items.

accent.$description: Fills only: the current-location point, balls, active marks.

accent-text.$description: Tomato when it has to be read as text.

on-accent.$description: Text on a filled tomato control, such as a hovered button. The fill is accent-text.

link.$description: Links. Teal, semibold, and always underlined.

link-hover.$description: Link text on hover; the underline turns tomato.

note.$description: Note and highlight fill. Pair with `text`.

flag.$description: A wall label hung over a figure, such as a card's Preprint. The same in both themes, since figures keep their colors. Pair with `flag-text`.

flag-edge.$description: The edge of a `flag`, so it keeps its shape on a pale figure.

focus.$description: Focus ring on the page ground.

selection.$description: Text selection, always with black text.

code-comment.$description: Code comments, in mustard light so explanations read first.

panel.$description: Panels sit lighter than the ground in dark mode.

viz.$description: Chart colors. Categorical slots are assigned in this order and never cycled. Validated for color vision deficiency with the dataviz palette checks (adjacent pairs). Scatter plots and small multiples use the first three slots only.

display.$description: Wood-type slab for titles, the wordmark, and big numerals. Never for running text.

text.$value: "Libre Franklin Variable", "Libre Franklin Fallback", Arial, sans-serif
text.$description: Everything that gets read: body, UI, captions, tables.

mono.$value: "JetBrains Mono Variable", "JetBrains Mono Fallback", Menlo, monospace
mono.$description: Code, keyboard keys, and numeric parameters.

xs.$description: 13px. Wall labels, tags, code bar text, and chart text.

sm.$description: 14px. Captions, hints, field labels, code blocks, and the on-this-page list.

ui.$description: Interface text: tabs, search, sidebar links, tables, notes, author lines.

md.$description: 16px. Buttons, inputs, and checkbox and switch labels.

body-wide.$description: 18px. The reading size of article and docs text from 100rem, where the page is at its widest.

xl.$description: 24px. Third-level headings, the wordmark, and pager titles.

3xl.$description: 44px. History wall numerals and paper titles on narrow screens.

4xl.$description: 64px. The top of the paper title range, the step below display.

display.$description: Page titles. 48px on phones up to 92px on wide screens.

regular.$description: Running text, and every use of Ultra, which has one weight.

medium.$description: Tabs, segmented controls, and the small label in the pager.

semibold.$description: Links, buttons, and the current tab.

bold.$description: Headings in Libre Franklin, field labels, wall labels, and strong text.

display.$description: Line height for Ultra display titles.

tight.$description: Line height for headings in Libre Franklin.

normal.$description: Line height for notes, captions, tables, and interface text.

relaxed.$description: Line height for running text in the reading column.

0.$description: No space. Not used by the kit; for resetting a gap in a scale-driven layout.

1.$description: 4px. The tightest gap, inside small groups such as a swatch and its value.

2.$description: 8px. Between a label and its field, and an icon and its text.

3.$description: 12px. Between items in a cluster, and below section headings.

4.$description: 16px. Between paragraphs, and the side gutter on phones.

5.$description: 24px. Panel padding and the side padding of buttons.

6.$description: 32px. Gaps between page columns and around figures.

7.$description: 48px. Above section headings and around the mast.

8.$description: 64px. Above the pager and the footnotes.

9.$description: 96px. Below the main column, before the footer.

10.$description: 128px. Not used by the kit; the largest step for very open layouts.

hair.$description: 1px. Rules between table rows and list items.

control.$description: 2px. Borders of buttons, inputs, and segmented controls.

rule.$description: The exhibit rule under the top bar and between page regions.

none.$description: Panels, buttons, inputs, and code blocks are square.

ball.$description: Only round things are round: balls, points, status dots.

drop.$description: One ball falling through the machine.

measure.$description: Reading column: about 68 characters of body text at 17px. Set in rem so notes, code, and text in one column share an edge.

measure-wide.$description: Reading column of article and docs pages from 100rem, where their text is 18px: still about 68 characters.

margin.$description: The margin after the reading column, for sidenotes and margin figures: its narrowest width. It opens when the main column has room for the measure, a 2rem gap, and this, and widens with the page to half again.

gutter.$description: Page side margin: 16px on phones, 72px on wide screens.

sidebar.$description: Width of the chapter sidebar of a docs page, shown from 56rem. The on-this-page list sits in it, under the current page.

toc.$description: Width of the on-this-page rail of an article page, shown from 80rem.
